claim_scope.statement: All games begin from the standard initial Progressive Series 1 with empty history; the engines own every played series. The 100-game schedule repeats one deterministic initial state, so its games are not independent opening samples.
claim_scope.warning: This is independent-engine game evidence, not calibrated Elo, a confidence interval, SPRT, equal-node evidence, an opening-general claim, or proof of universal Stockfish-level strength.

common_control.clock_scope: local analyze call versus Bucephalus process start, history replay, and search

local_limits.best_settings_meaning: the best-settings label means the frozen D8/W32/16-thread/120s search configuration; not proof this evaluator profile is strongest
local_limits.deadline_result: safety-certified-completed-series-or-technical-incomplete; UNKNOWN/deadline/work-limit candidate safety withholding never permits legal-move fallback; a different root may publish only after its own exact final immediate and applicable ladder gates

neural_s3_ordering.scope: Black Series 2 complete boundaries entering Series 3 only
neural_s3_ordering.strength_claim: frozen ordering configuration; no prior proof of strongest profile

local_limits.selected_move_safety: an UNKNOWN candidate never publishes; a different root may publish only after its own exact final immediate and applicable ladder gates; otherwise technical incomplete

equivalence_check.scope: initial position, exact completed PLY 1 through 4

instrumentation.purpose: flush each completed iterative-deepening PLY record before the external wall-clock deadline
instrumentation.semantic_change: add fflush(stdout) immediately after each completed PLY line

profile.name: Scottish Progressive baseline
profile.notes: Hand-authored reference profile; no match-strength claim.

local_engine.profile_approval_meaning: frozen baseline profile identity only; not a playing-strength claim

resources.ram_note: memory_per_worker is a conservative planning estimate, not an operating-system process memory limit

rule_and_protocol_gaps.impact: No FEN/setboard protocol; every call starts a new process and replays a canonical history from the orthodox initial board.

Both engines receive the same per-move wall ceiling. The local engine returns its deepest completed series-depth iteration, or a move-only fallback only after exact required reply and selected-root ladder safety checks. Unknown safety withholds the move and is retained as a technical incomplete. Bucephalus uses the frozen output-only v4 completion controller: a replay-validated PLY1 anchor, live deep search, and replay-validated suffix continuation. Every selected move was emitted by the pinned engine; process stops, restarts, stitching, and anchor fallback are disclosed.
Local depth counts complete progressive series; Bucephalus depth counts individual micro-moves. Results are fixed-policy performance evidence, not equal-node or equal-depth evidence.

Bucephalus has no ten-quiet-series draw and scores an internally detected stalemate by material. The harness adjudicates only the authoritative result after replay, but its search choices retain that rule-evaluation mismatch.
Upstream uses an unchecked 100-move array, a 200-entry replay record, and a 30-micro-ply ceiling. Root/replay limits are guarded; deeper search-array overflow remains an upstream risk.
Worker planning reserves about 191 MiB for each external process, but the operating system does not enforce a per-process RAM ceiling.
